question: In ICD-11, gender incongruence is classified as a mental disorder under Chapter 06 (Mental, Behavioural or Neurodevelopmental Disorders), retaining its earlier ICD-10 classification.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. A key ICD-11 change specifically relevant to transgender patients is that gender incongruence was relocated FROM the mental disorders chapter TO Chapter 17 (Conditions Related to Sexual Health). Homosexuality per se was already removed from ICD as a disorder in ICD-10 (1990). These are two distinct reclassification events with different clinical implications.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is false. ICD-11 moved gender incongruence OUT of the mental disorders chapter. It is now classified under Chapter 17 (Conditions Related to Sexual Health) as 'HA60 — Gender incongruence of adolescence or adulthood' and 'HA61 — Gender incongruence of childhood'. This reclassification acknowledges that gender diversity is not a mental disorder while retaining a diagnostic category to enable access to gender-affirming healthcare.
